full_judgment:
Mr. Mir Hashmat Ali, J: This Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the Respondents to show cause as to why the impugned Order No. 15 dated 03.02.2005 and decree dated 10.02.2005 passed by the learned Artha Rin Adalat, Court No. 2, Bagerhat in Artha Rin Case No. 33 of 2004 whereby the case was disposed of on the basis of the report submitted by the settler and issued a certificate under section 22(10) of the Artha Rin Adalat  Ain, 2003 in favour of the plaintiff Bank vide Annexure-'A' and 'A-1' should not be declared to have been passed without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 3. The Artha Rin Suit No. 33 of 2004 was taken up for exparte disposal on 03.02.2005 and exparte decreed the suit, accordingly on 10.02.21305 decree was signed. The plaintiff decree holder started execution Case No.58 of 2005 before the Artha Rin Adalat and Joint District Judge, Bagerhat on 27.06.2005. 4. The plaintiff case in short is that, M/s. Barishal Store a business firm and the petitioner-defendant is the Proprietor of the said business firm, The Janata Bank granted a C.C. Loan of Tk. 8,00,000/- vide Sanction letter No. অগ্রীম/সি.সি/৪৫/০১ dated 08.08.2001. As a security for the C.C. loan the petitioner executed different deeds and security, the ' petitioner executed a mortgage deed in respect of land described in the schedule and ' the petitioner re-paid the same in time and thereafter the Janata Bank again granted a C.C. loan of Tk. 8,00,000/- vide Memo No. অগ্রীম/সি.সি/৪৮/০২ dated 17.06.2002 and the defendant received of Tk. 10,12,157/-. Though the petitioner obtained profit from the business but he did not pay up the loan. Though the plaintiff requested for payment of loan along with interest up to 17.03.2004 A to the tune of Tk.9,77,848/- only. The plaintiff served legal notice but the defendant does not pay and hence the Artha Rin Suit. 

 5. The defendant-petitioner appeared and submitted written statement on 30.08.2004 stating that earlier loan has already been paid and adjusted in time but the plaintiff with ill motive continued the said loan in this account. It was further asserted in the written statement that on 17.06.2002 C.C. 4; loan was granted up to Tk. 8,00,000/- but the plaintiff most illegally stated that the defendant withdrawn Tk. 10,12,157/-. The trial Court after framing the issues, suo-moto fixed on 22.09.2004 for effecting compromise vide order dated 13.09.2004 and appointed the teamed Advocate for that effect and the next date was fixed on 24.10.2004 for report.) The defendant subsequently came to know on 17.07.2005 that decree has been passed on 03.02.2005 under Section 44 of the Artha Rio Adalat AM, 2003. Consequently, the defendant-petitioner on 08.08.2005 filed an application r, under Section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Aim 2003 for setting aside the said decree dated 03.02.2005 along with an application on the ground that a fraud has been committed in the order dated 03.02.2005 and as such the duty of the trial Court Is to set aside the same but without hearing the said application or without disposing of the said application started execution proceeding. It was further stated though the application under Section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain has been filed before the Artha Rin Adalat but no order has been passed by the said Adalat. 

 7. Mr. S. N. Goswami, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that no notice was served upon the petitioner by the learned Advocate for effecting compromise. He further submits that learned Advocate for the petitioner obtained a signature under a verification for other purpose but such verification has been used as compromise petition. He further submits that according to Sub section 4 of Section 21 of the Artha Rin Adalat AM, 2003 there should be a meeting between the parties and execute an agreement for effecting compromise and after the execution of the agreement the settler shall submit a report along with the agreement. Both the parties required to be signed in the said agreement and the learned Advocates of both the parties should also signed as witness to the compromise agreement and -after the said compromise the decree will be passed according to Order 23 of the Code of Civil Procedure. But in the instant case the compromise petition annexure-W to the writ petition shows that no agreement was effected and both the parties has not signed in the said report of the settler and none of the plaintiffs has been signed in the said report and as such the said report can not be construed as an agreement having under the term and conditions of agreement. He further submits that ,176710 which was mentioned in the said report of the settler shows that the petitioner has signed in the said paper in the chamber of his learned Advocate not before the settler and as such a fraud has been committed upon the petitioner. He further submits that even if for argument sake a settlement has been made; the decree if any should be passed in accordance with Order 23 of the Code of Civil Procedure. But in the instant case decree has been passed under Section 44 of the Artha Rin Adalat AM. He further submits that under Section 44 of the Artha Rin Adalat AM ad-interim order can be passed but not a decree and as such the order passed by Artha Rin Adalat on 03.02.2005 is an order but not a decree and as such it is amenable under the writ jurisdiction. He further submits that no notice was served upon the defendant-petitioner by the settler. But the plaintiff in connivance with the learned Advocate for the petitioner fraudulently used the ,137,105 Of the petitioner executed for other purpose in the chamber of the learned Advocate petitioner. He further submits that the defendant-petitioner never appeared before the settler as no notice was issued and served upon him by the settler. He further submits that at the time of passing the alleged order/ decree; Rule 3 of order 23 of the Code of Civil Procedure has not been observed and complied with; which indicate that the agreement which may form part of the decree is not a lawful order. In the instant case the decree is not lawful and that the Court below violated the mandatory provisions of Section 22 and 24 of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. He further submits that for effecting compromise according to the Section 24 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain; the Board of directors of the plaintiff-Bank should pass a resolution to that effect but in the instant case no such resolution has been taken by the Artha Rin Adalat is without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect. In support of his contention, he cited the case of Government of Bangladesh-Vs-Ministry of Home Affairs and another passed in Sao mom Rule No.02 of 2007, the case of Hossain All Khan-Vs-Firoza Begum reported in 21 DLR-9. He further submits that the order dated 03.02.2005 is a misconceived order and under Section 44 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain no decree can be passed and as such decree is not lawful decree and amenable to the writ jurisdiction. He further submits that after the order dated 03.02.2005 the petitioner filed an application under Section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat AM but the Court below passed no order though the Adalat received the application. 

 8. Mr. Mamunur Rashid, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent-Bank submits that since the decree has been passed against the respondent-petitioner the remedy lies in filing the appeal against such decree and no writ petition is maintainable even if the decree is illegal. In support of his contention, he cited the case of Zahirul Islam - Vs National Bank Ltd. And others reported in 46 DLR (AL))- 191, the case of Gazi M. Towfic-VsAgrani Bank and others reported in 54 DLR(AD)-6, the case of - Bangladesh Agricultural Development Corporation (BADC) Vs- Artha Rin Adalat AM and others reported in 59 DLR (AD)-6. 

 10. It appears from the writ petition that Respondent No. 2, Janata Bank as plaintiff instituted Artha Rin Case No. 33 of 2004 before the Court of Artha Rin Adalat, Court No. 2, Bagerhat for realization of Tk. 10,12,157/- against the defendant-petitioner stating that the defendant-petitioner took loan against C.C. Account No. 45 of 2001 amounting to Tk.8,00,000/-. At the time of taking loan the defendant-petitioner executed mortgage deed in favour of the Bank on 12.04.2001 and 19.04.2001. Subsequently, after payment of entire dues the defendant-petitioner again prayed for loan and the plaintiff-respondent No. 2 again on 17.06.2002 vide Memo No. অগ্রীম/সি.সি/৮৪/০২ granted joint C.C. loan of Tk. 8,00,000/-. The plaintiff demanded repayment of the loan. At the time of filing of the Artha Rin Suit; the entire claim was Tk. 10,12,175. It appears that the defendant-petitioner appeared and submitted written statement. The Artha Rin Adalat on 13.09.2004 fixed the date for compromise between the parties and Advocate Shapan Kumar Deb was engaged as settler and 24.10.2004 was fixed for report. But on 24.10.2004 no report was submitted before the Artha Rin Adalat. Next date was fixed on 24.11.2004. The settler, the learned Advocate filed an application for adjournment. The prayer was allowed and the date was fixed on 30.11.2004. On 30.11.2004 the settler learned Advocate filed an application for adjournment. The prayer was allowed and on 06.01.2005 was fixed for filing report in Court. On 06.01.2005 the settler learned Advocate took no steps and the trial Court found that the settler failed to make any compromise and fixed on 03.02.2005 for hearing of the suit, On the date fixed for hearing of the- suit on 03.02.2005 the settler submitted a report, The Artha Rin Adalat accepted the report and decreed the suit under Section 44 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain according, to the report of  the settler. Let us see the report of the settler, which runs thus: 

 Which shows that he has signed the document in the chamber of his learned Advocate and in presence of the learned Advocate and as such we find that the signature was neither made before the settler nor in his chamber. It further appears that none of the plaintiff signed in the said settlement. According to Section 24 of Artha Rin Adalat AM for effecting the settlement the Board of Directors may take a resolution and authorize any officer or any other competent person for effecting the compromise. In the instant case, we do not find any such endorsement nor any person for the plaintiff signed in the settlement. It appears from the report of the settler that no endorsement was made by the plaintiff-respondent No. 2 as required under Section 24 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. It further appears from the record that the report does not appear to be an agreement to the terms and conditions as required under Sub-section (4) of Section 21 of the Artha Rin Adalat AM. It further appears that the decree should be passed under Order 23 of the Code of Civil Procedure. But in the instant case decree was passed under 

 And as such we find that no decree can be passed under Section 44 of the Artha Rin Adalat AM. The Artha Rin Adalat most erroneously and illegally passed the decree and Section 44 does not empower the Adalat to pass any decree against any person. It has been held in the case of Mir Motiur Rahman Zihadi -Vs- Artha Rin Adalat, Tangail and another reported in 15 BLT(AD)-267, that A judgment-debtor is not competent to challenge the decree of the Artha Rin Adalat in writ jurisdiction unless the judgment and decree of the Adalat is without jurisdiction or in other words coram non judice or outcome of fraud committed on Court and that also suffers from 'malafide. It has been held in the case of Md. Arfan Uddin Akand and another -Vs- Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No.1, Gazipur and another reported in 15 BLT(HCD)-343. 

 12. It has also been held in the case of Hossain Ali Khan -Vs- Firoza Begum reported in 21 DLR-9, that "Rule 3 Order XXIII of the Code of Civil Procedure clearly indicates that the agreement which may form part of the decree must be lawful and if it is contrary to law, a court cannot pass a decree in accordance with such an agreement." 

 13. We have observed that the report submitted by the settler is not an agreement in accordance with law as both the parties has not signed in the agreement and such an agreement cannot be form part of the decree according to order 3 of Rule 23 of the Code of Civil Procedure. No body dispute that against the decree passed by Artha Rin Adalat the remedy lies an appeal. But in the instant case the Artha Rin Adalat passed the decree on an unlawful agreement and that the decree was passed under Section 44 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain and as such, such decree is without jurisdiction and as such the judgment and decree dated 03.02.2005 is amenable under the writ jurisdiction. 

 14. The impugned Order No. 15 dated 03.02.2005 and the decree thereof dated 10.02.2005 passed by Artha Rin Adalat, Court No.2, Bagerhat in Artha Rin Case No. 33 of 2004 is declared to have been made and passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. However, the suit is remanded to the Trial Court for fresh trial in accordance with law.
